newsitem.title: UK: Virgin chosen for UK West Coast rail line.
newsitem.headline: Virgin chosen for UK West Coast rail line.

text.p: British entrepreneur Richard Branson's Virgin Group has been selected to run the InterCity West Coast (ICWC) passenger rail franchise.

Britain's franchising director John O'Brien of the Office of Passenger Rail Franchising (Opraf) announced Virgin Rail's selection late on Friday, adding a formal announcement with further details of the deal would be made soon.
The West Coast line is the last of Britain's major rail routes to be sold off under the government's privatisation of the national rail system.
ICWC operates passenger rail services between London's Euston station and the West Midlands, north Wales and the north-west of England and Scotland.
Last November it emerged that three companies had been shortlisted to operate the line, Sea Containers Ltd and Stagecoach Holdings Plc competing with Virgin for the franchise.
Sea Containers already runs the East Coast mainline which runs between London and Edinburgh and the east of Scotland.
The Financial Times newspaper said on Saturday the award of the 15-year franchise for Britain's busiest railway to Virgin would "make Virgin a powerful competitor with the domestic airline".

If confirmed as successful, Virgin would spend 600 million pounds to introduce tilting trains on the 550 mile route and a further 1.5 billion pounds would be spent by Railtrack on improving track and signalling, the paper added.
Sunday's Observer newspaper said Virgin had asked for "as little as 400 million pounds of public subsidy to win the contest". It said the winning bid was likely to be confirmed within two weeks.

Virgin has already won control of the the CrossCountry service, which covers more than 130 stations and is based in the central city of Birmingham. It said it would spend an extra 250 million pounds on new trains and increased services on the CrossCountry line.
Virgin has also bid for the Thameslink service in London.
